title: Nammos
meta_description: Nammos is a concept campaign for the Mykonos beach club, testing whether the turquoise-and-white stripe alone can carry the brand once the club, the crowd and the coastline are taken away.
deck: A self-directed campaign for Nammos, whose umbrellas are the most recognisable thing about it. So the campaign keeps the stripe and removes everything else: no club, no crowd, no shoreline. One striped object on open water, and the brand still arrives.

proof.title: The stripe is the whole logo.
proof.note: Nammos is sold everywhere as a room full of people. That is the one thing a spec ad cannot borrow, and the one thing the club does not actually need: the turquoise-and-white stripe is doing the identifying long before a single face is legible. Each frame here is a test of that, with the object placed far out in flat water where nothing else can help it.

shots.alt: A turquoise-and-white striped beach umbrella standing in shallow open sea, sheltering two people in white who sit on plastic chairs reading newspapers, with distant hills on the horizon.
shots.caption: Frame 01 / the umbrella, kept and nothing else

shots.alt: Overhead view of a turquoise-and-white striped floating mattress adrift on deep blue water, a woman asleep under white bedding at one end.
shots.caption: Frame 02 / the sunbed, off its row

shots.alt: A striped mug and an open book on a weathered blue table at the edge of the sea, a ginger cat asleep across the pages beside an empty chair.
shots.caption: Frame 03 / the stripe on a mug, and no one to serve

proof.caption: Nothing in these frames is doing hospitality. The chairs are plastic, the reading material is a newspaper, the table is peeling, and the guest is a cat. The turquoise survives all of it, which is the finding: the stripe is the asset, and the luxury it implies is added by the viewer.

acts.title: Three reels, one stripe.
acts.note: The set runs from the object everyone recognises to the object nobody would notice, so the test gets harder rather than more flattering as it goes.

items.title: The umbrella
items.copy: The canopy planted in open water with the beach deleted. Two guests, dressed for the club, reading as though the sea were a terrace.

items.title: The sunbed
items.copy: A single striped mattress adrift, seen from above. The bed that is only ever photographed in a row of eighty, alone.

items.title: The mug
items.copy: The stripe reduced to a piece of crockery on a peeling table, holding the frame with a sleeping cat and no service in sight.

pipeline.title: Pipeline.
pipeline.note: Made with no brief and no client, which is why the constraint could be this severe: every frame had to be readable as Nammos with the club withheld.

items.label: Sample
items.copy: The stripe pinned first as a fixed width and a fixed turquoise, so the umbrella, the mattress and the mug are all carrying the same swatch.

items.label: Strip
items.copy: Coastline, architecture, staff and crowd cut from every composition, leaving one branded object and water.

items.label: Stage
items.copy: The horizon held at the same height across the set, so three unrelated scenes read as one location.

items.label: Grade
items.copy: Sea and sky desaturated toward haze so the turquoise is the only saturated colour left in frame.

items.label: Move
items.copy: Each still animated to a 9:16 reel with the camera almost static, because the joke only lands if the scene is calm enough to be believed.
